analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied (documentation, no executable code), so none of the described behavior could be verified against source. The head entries describe security-relevant changes in these areas:
- Prefix cache and SSD (T-041): demanded prefix checkpoint capture and retention (head lines 8-16), first-appearance SSD write share for repeated checkpoints (line 11), short-prefix capture below the solo stripe (line 13), and SSD write-budget enforcement (lines 72-73). These could affect the per-donation adoption/benefit gate; the code was not reviewed. Cache scoping is described as unchanged.
- Autopilot floor rewards (T-060, T-059): consent journaling made concurrent, reward authorization evaluated at the declaration's server receive time, floor accrual ending 2026-11-07, payments default off, and baseline repair endpoints (head lines 3-5, 23-33). The text says it preserves erasure fences and sponsored-inference accounting.
- Account erasure and soft-delete gating (T-059): the soft-delete mutation gate is default off and production env refresh preserves opt-ins (lines 107-112).
- Other described changes: PII removed from coordinator logs (T-051, T-058; line 142-144), the Bedrock review and merge-clearance workflow, and the Stripe withdrawal queue.
The next pass should check these against the source if code is supplied. Key places: the SSD donation gate in SSDPrefixCache.donate, the consent-journal locking and erasure fences, and the admin baseline-repair authorization.

findings.detail: The new changelog entries say authenticated repeated checkpoints get the reserved SSD write share on their first local appearance. They also say short repeated prefixes below the normal solo stripe are now captured and published for reuse. T-041's detection_hint says loosening the per-donation gate (adoption bound plus 1,024-token benefit floor) widens the at-rest surface and needs review. T-041 also still says the SSD tier caches only adoptable long prefixes. If these demanded checkpoints reach SSD donation without meeting that gate, short prefixes would be written to disk and become probeable through the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035) for the 30-minute TTL. This is a documentation-level concern: the code is not in this batch, so I cannot confirm whether the gate applies. Fix: confirm the demanded-checkpoint path still passes the SSD adoption/benefit gate, then update T-041 and its detection_hint to record the demanded-capture path and its sign-off.
findings.title: Demanded-prefix SSD write sharing may widen T-041's per-donation gate without a sign-off
